body: The screenshot changes nothing: taking a shot of a painted canvas runs no step and changes no document, focus or tree state.
The screenshot's contract stands: an 800 by 600 shot over opaque white, byte-identical across processes on one host, fonts-unavailable before anything is painted, with a canvas now painted into it.
A password input is still painted masked in every shot; the password text is never revealed by any new paint path.

Pixels as a content class: option labels of an open list leave only as pixels by a ratified widening; a canvas's app-painted content leaving through the screenshot answer is a widening of its own, a fork for the operator, not a default.
The driver's screenshot verb, its element shot and its open-list row shot keep their answers; no new verb, argument, carrier, cause, refusal or session error unless a fork's ruling adds one.

The build feature change that turns the custom-widget paint on in every selection must not pull a platform accessibility adapter into any stand binary nor change which accessibility features are on by default.
The session library keeps accessibility enabled and the snapshot readers stay behind the accessibility feature in every build selection after the feature change.

The stand's served tasks keep their snapshot, lint and actions readings; the stand reads no lint finding at boot and its contrast assertions hold, re-recorded only if a ruling moves one, never loosened.
If the stand gains a canvas page or task (an operator fork), its readings join the stand's expectation tables, contrast, focus order and lint checks like every served task.
Contrast is left unread past non-colour paint: a canvas's painted scene is not read as a text colour pair by the lint or the harness contrast reader.

The adapter tree equals the harness tree and the snapshot reads the accessibility tree: a canvas host element enters the tree by the same role and name rules as any element, with no canvas-specific tree reading added.
Every new check runs in both layout modes (incremental and non-incremental) and is shown red first with its red reading kept in evidence.
Every build, test and CI cargo leg passes the locked flag; no new crate or dependency beyond a taken fork; the accessibility CI leg and the gate it holds still pass.
No content in a log field and no new log field or span: a canvas's painted content never reaches a log line.

Makes what an app paints from Rust, through blitz-dom's Widget trait and its recorded scene, appear in a headless shot: the harness's screenshot and screenshot_rect on the CPU buffer, the driver's screenshot verb that rides it, and the escher-session binary's screenshot.
Measures on the stand first, before any fix: the stand boots a canvas and a shot of it is taken and read, in both layout modes, under each build selection the project runs it in.
Makes a shot paint a widget in every build selection (harness, driver, seven_guis and the escher-session binary alike, not only a workspace build), so a check's reading does not hang on which packages a cargo invocation selected.
Shows every check it adds red first, on the tree before its fix or with the fix reverted, its red reading kept beside its green.
Re-asserts the screenshot contract and the stand's served-task readings, committed kept checks and stand checks unchanged unless an operator ruling moves one.

the scene painter's custom-widget feature and its building of the custom widget scenes behind that feature
the scene painter's drawing of a custom widget's recorded scene into the page's scene
the harness screenshot — screenshot and screenshot_rect rendered to a CPU buffer, the shot the driver's screenshot verb rides
the Dioxus mutation writer that hands a custom widget to the document from an object element's data attribute; a canvas element's paint source is parsed and read by nothing

body: The harness screenshot and screenshot_rect, rendered on the CPU buffer, show the pixels a custom widget paints through the Widget trait's recorded scene.
The driver session's screenshot verb and the escher-session screenshot command and MCP screenshot tool result, which ride the harness shot, carry the widget's painted pixels in band.

The scene painter's custom-widget feature is on in every per-package build selection the project runs (harness, driver, seven_guis, escher-session binary, blitz-tests), not only in a workspace build; a per-package green is not the workspace green.
Measured on the stand first: the seven_guis headless stand boots a canvas and its shot is taken and read before any fix, in both layout modes, under each build selection.
Every check the chunk adds is controlled red-before-green: run red on the tree before the fix or with the fix reverted, its red reading kept in the chunk's evidence beside the green.

The screenshot contract stands: an 800 x 600 shot over opaque white, its PNG byte-identical across processes on one host, refused fonts-unavailable before anything is painted, a password input painted masked, no step run and nothing changed by a shot.
No new verb, argument, carrier, refusal cause, session error, exit code, log field or span unless an operator fork ruling adds one; no screen content in any log line, stderr line or span field.

App-painted canvas content leaving through the screenshot answer on the session socket, the command line, MCP and a kept check's shot record is an operator fork (a content class of its own beside a shot's pixels and an open select list's labels); committed recorded checks keep holding no screenshot step.

The stand's seven served tasks keep their cross-OS snapshot, lint and actions digests, and the committed kept checks and stand checks keep their readings; a ruling that moves one re-records it, never loosens it; cross-OS byte comparisons hold no shot.

Which element hosts a canvas (an object element's data as upstream's Dioxus path stands, or a canvas element nothing wires) and whether the stand gains a canvas page or task are operator forks, never answered by a default.
The CPU renderer's custom-paint gap stays out: a widget painting through a texture or a resource is not made to show; no web Canvas 2D context and no wgpu canvas.
Every build, test and CI cargo leg passes --locked; no new crate or dependency beyond what a taken fork names.
Stand checks run on the bundled pinned font with no skip, offline, and hold their zero-failure budget across the three stand-repeat rounds.
Every requirement the chunk adds is witnessed inside stand-repeat, and a capability claim for the canvas names its checks (whether this chunk claims v040-09 is read at P4).

body_fields.convention: each new integration test file is a target of its own, one behaviour per target, and a shared module it uses is no target
each new test's expected value is pinned as a literal, and its failure prints no argument value
each new test's data and fixtures are stated in code, nothing seeded, shared fixtures and stand tables in one module
each new check reads no wall clock and sleeps never; time moves only by the virtual clock
each new pixel test reads a CPU buffer and decodes its PNG in the check, comparing frames whole
each new stand-in is hand-written, no mocking library
each new code path is held by the per-crate line coverage floors and the zero-failure budget for stand checks
